CausalChain: Aberrant expression of dual‐localized lncRNAs -> Binding to chromatin modifiers in the nucleus and mitochondrial transcription regulators -> Coordinated dysregulation of nuclear gene expression and mitochondrial metabolism -> Altered reactive oxygen species production and apoptotic thresholds -> Enhanced tumor survival and metastasis
Hypothesis: Dual‐localized lncRNAs function as integrative regulators linking nuclear epigenetic programming to mitochondrial metabolic activity. Modulating these lncRNAs will disrupt cancer cells' metabolic adaptability and increase their sensitivity to apoptosis, thereby reducing tumor progression and metastasis.
Abstract: Recent advances in the study of long non‐coding RNAs (lncRNAs) have expanded our understanding of their spatial and functional complexity. Emerging evidence points to a subset of lncRNAs that are not confined to a single compartment but shuttle between the nucleus and mitochondria, thereby potentially coordinating nuclear gene regulation with mitochondrial energy metabolism. In this hypothesis, we propose that these dual‐localized lncRNAs act as integrative sensors that modulate chromatin structure and mitochondrial transcriptome dynamics simultaneously. Their interactions with chromatin remodelers and mitochondrial transcription factors may regulate key metabolic and apoptotic pathways, thereby contributing to tumor cell survival and metastatic potential. Targeting these dual‐localized lncRNAs could perturb the metabolic flexibility of cancer cells and sensitize them to apoptosis, offering a novel avenue for precision therapeutic intervention.
